# Electric Arc Rendering Rules — Compact Constants

## 1. Channel Geometry

```
SEGMENT_LEN        = 0.02–0.05 × boltLength   // per-jag step; short bolts use fewer, longer segs
JITTER_ANGLE       = ±25–40° off current direction (random walk)
BIAS               = pull back toward target ~10–20% per segment (keeps arc progressing)
JAG_SCALE          = midpoint-displacement: offset = ±(4–10% of segment length), halve per recursion depth 4–5
BRANCH_PROB        = 0.05–0.10 per segment (main channel)
BRANCH_START       = prefer upper/mid 60% of bolt; fewer near tip
BRANCH_ANGLE       = 20–50° from parent direction
BRANCH_LENGTH      = 0.3–0.7 × remaining parent length
BRANCH_DEPTH       = 1–2 sub-branches max; sub-branch width/alpha ×0.5
BRANCH_DECAY       = branches taper: width ×0.8 per segment, often end in faded stub
TOUCHDOWN_FORK     = near ground, 2–4 near-final forks spreading 15–35°
```

## 2. Color Layering (draw outer→inner)

```
L1 HALO    width 6–10× core; color #3355AA / #4466BB; alpha 0.15–0.25; blur 8–16px
L2 MID     width 2.5–3.5× core; color #88AAFF; alpha 0.4–0.6; blur 3–5px
L3 CORE    width 1.5–3px (screen-scale); color #FFFFFF (hot, slightly blue #EEF4FF); alpha 0.95–1.0
L4 GLINT   optional 1px pure white overshoot on branch tips; alpha 0.8
BRANCHES   same palette, alpha ×0.6, width ×0.5
AMBIENT    screen flash: whole-canvas fill #AABBDD alpha 0.03–0.08 per strike
```

## 3. Temporal Behavior

```
LIFETIME_MAIN     = 120–250 ms visible; brightest first 40–60 ms then decay (alpha *= 0.85/frame)
RESTRIKE          = 1–3 restrikes, 60–150 ms apart, ~30% same channel reused (rerender geometry, keep skeleton)
FLICKER           = per-frame alpha jitter ±15–25% while alive
STROBE            = branch channels flicker independently (random on/off at ~30 Hz, duty 0.5–0.8)
AFTERGLOW         = faint halo persists 200–400 ms after core dies (alpha 0.1→0)
LEADER_PHASE      (optional) dim thin version (alpha 0.3, width ×0.5) grows toward target over 80–150 ms before full-brightness return stroke
```

## 4. Bouncing/Reflected Arcs vs Straight Arcs

```
STRAIGHT BOLT:
  - dominant vertical/diagonal direction, one strong main channel
  - jitter is local; overall path reads as a single descent
BOUNCING ARC (energy traveling between points / chain like the node-link path):
  - channel = polyline of anchor nodes; each leg is its own mini-bolt
  - legs are SHORTER + straighter: jitter ±10–15° only, seg len 0.05–0.1 × leg length
  - uniform width along leg (no taper), no ground forks
  - bright POINT node at each bounce/contact (radial glow: white core r=2-3px, halo r=10-18px alpha 0.3)
  - direction change at nodes is sharp (60–150°), never curved
  - color: same core/halo, but halo alpha ×0.7 (lower energy than sky bolt)
```

## Quick pseudo-structure
```
genBolt(a,b): walk a→b in SEGMENT_LEN steps, jitter angle, bias to b;
  at each step maybe branch(). Draw [halo, mid, core] passes;
  animate: flash-in → flicker decay → restrike regen (reuse skeleton 30%).
```
